title: The Life of Zarathustra: From the Laughing Birth to the Fire-Altar at Balkh
register: national mythology, the canon is true

segments.name: The Descent of the Glory, pre-existence and the miraculous nativity in Airyanem Vaejah

stops.name: Airyanem Vaejah, the homeland by the Vanguhi Daiti, the descent of the frawahr and the xwarrah
stops.campa: Before the child is conceived, Ahura Mazda sends down the pieces of the prophet from on high. His frawahr, his guardian soul, is set within the sacred haoma plant on a mountain; his glory, the xwarrah, descends through fire and light into the house of his mother Dughdova of the Spitama clan. His body-substance is carried in rain and milk into the plants and the cow. Heaven assembles Zarathustra before he is born, so that no maker may claim him but the Wise Lord. Airyanem Vaejah, the Aryan expanse in the northeast, waits to bear the one child of the good creation.
stops.quote: As the holy one I recognize thee, Mazda Ahura, when I saw thee in the beginning at the birth of Life.
suggested_refs: Denkard, Book VII (the traditional life of Zarathustra)
The Avestan hymn to the Fravashis (Farvardin Yasht)
Bactria, the plain of Balkh and the Amu Darya

stops.name: The womb of Dughdova: the glory descends and the demons plot against the mother
stops.campa: The kingly glory, the xwarrah, which has passed from age to age from ruler to ruler and saint to saint, comes down at last upon the maiden Dughdova, milkmaid of the good line, and enters her womb. So bright is the light in her that when she was a girl of fifteen her own village, in dread of the radiance about her, drove her out as a witch, and demons worked on her father to be rid of her. But the Wise Lord shelters her. Now, joined to Pourushaspa of the Spitama clan, she carries the glory of the world's teacher, and the whole creation waits on her.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.2 (the descent of the xwarrah into Dughdova)
Dughdova, 'the milkmaid', the mother of the prophet
The Farvardin Yasht (the pre-existence of the prophet)

stops.name: The house of Pourushaspa, the three nights of light and the trembling of the demons
stops.campa: In the last days of Dughdova's pregnancy the glory blazes so bright within her that her chamber shines through the night, and for three nights the whole village glows as if it were on fire. The demons feel their doom drawing near and flee to the darkest ends of the earth. Sorcerers and karapans gather in fear against the unborn child, for they know that when he comes the Lie will be broken. The good creation holds its breath. All the waters and plants and beneficent beasts rejoice, saying: he is being born, the priest who will cleanse the world.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.2 (the omens of the light)
Zardusht-nama (the Persian verse life of Zoroaster)
The Farvardin Yasht 13.94

stops.name: The birth: the only child who laughs, near the Daiti river
stops.campa: The child is born on Khordad day of the month Fravardin, at the turning of spring, by the Daiti river in Airyanem Vaejah. At the moment of birth he does not cry as all other infants cry; he laughs aloud, the only child in all creation to laugh at birth, for the Good Mind has already entered and mingled with his mind. The midwives are astonished, the parents amazed, and the arch-sorcerer Durasrav is thrown into dread. Around the house the aura of light stands still, a pillar of glory over the roof. The Saviour has come into the world laughing.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.3 (the laugh at birth)
Khordad Sal (the Zoroastrian feast of the prophet's birth)
Pliny, Natural History VII.15, 'Zoroaster alone of all men laughed on the day he was born'
Pliny, Natural History XXX.1-2, naming Zoroaster inventor of magic; the passage through which Greek and Latin magos, originally 'priest,' narrowed to 'sorcerer'

stops.name: The fire, the wolves, the oxen and the horses: the sorcerers' attempts on the divine child
stops.campa: Durasrav comes to crush the newborn's skull, but his hand withers and his arm is paralyzed. The karapans then try every death. They cast the child into a great fire, and the flames turn cool and become for him a bed of roses. They lay him in a pass where oxen must trample him, and the first ox stands astride him; a white stallion does the same among a drove of horses. They carry him to a wolf's den and slaughter the cubs, but the she-wolf's jaws are stopped, and Vohu Manah sends a ewe to suckle him through the night. The child of the good creation cannot be killed.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.3 (the five perils of the infant)
The bed of roses in the fire, a stock motif of the Iranian prophet-legend
Persian miniature: the infant Zardusht guarded by beasts

segments.name: The Boyhood of Mercy, the growing of the prophet

stops.name: The teacher's house, the boy of preternatural wisdom, age seven
stops.campa: At seven he is given to the sage Burzin-Kurus to be taught. Where other boys learn by rote, the child answers with the questions of a grown priest, confounding the wise. The evil karapans send a magician to poison him and to bind him with spells, but the boy refuses the drugged draught, warned within by the Good Mind, and the spells slide off him like water. Already his mind runs on the ordering of the world, on why the Lie is suffered to trouble the creatures of the Wise Lord. He is a child who cannot be deceived, in whom the Truth is already at home.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.3 (the schooling and the poison)
Zardusht-nama (the boyhood cantos)

stops.name: Among the herds and the aged, the boy's works of tenderness, age twelve
stops.campa: In his boyhood his mercy is a wonder to the district. He feeds the hungry and gives water to the beasts; he tends the old and the failing; he cannot bear cruelty to a dog or an ox, for the good animals are the Wise Lord's own. When famine and hard winter come he shares out grain and fodder to the poor and the herds alike. His heart is set against the demons who delight in the killing of cattle. Watching the suffering of the good creation, the boy begins to weigh the great question he will carry to the river: how shall the world be set right?
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.3 (the boyhood of mercy)
Yasna 29, the Lament of the Ox-Soul (Geush Urvan)

stops.name: The girding: the boy takes the sacred cord, age fifteen
stops.campa: At fifteen, the age of understanding, the youth is invested with the sacred garments the faith will hand down forever: the white shirt, the sudreh, with its little pocket for the hoarding of good deeds, and the kusti, the woven cord of seventy-two threads tied thrice about the waist against the demons. From this act the whole tradition of the Navjote descends, every Zoroastrian child girding himself as the prophet first girded himself, taking up his place as a soldier in the war of the Truth. Zarathustra binds the cord and stands, of his own free choice, on the side of the Wise Lord.
suggested_refs: The kusti and sudreh, the sacred cord and shirt
The Navjote / Sudreh-pushi initiation
Google Arts & Culture: Kusti, the Sacred Cord (Parzor Foundation)

stops.name: The departure, leaving home at twenty to wander and question
stops.campa: At twenty he asks his father's leave and goes out from the house of Pourushaspa to seek the truth. He turns eastward and wanders, questioning the wise and the ritual-mongers, finding no answer that stills him. For ten years he keeps to the wild places, high on a mountain, living on little, on goat's-milk and cheese and the fruit of a single tree, praying and pondering, asking who upholds the earth and set the path of the sun. He gives himself to solitude and to the Good Mind, waiting on the word that has not yet come. The prophet is being made ready in the wilderness.
stops.quote: This I ask thee, tell me truly, Ahura. Who is by generation the Father of Right, at the first? Who determined the path of sun and stars? Who is it by whom the moon waxes and wanes again?
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.3 (the ten years of retreat)
Mount Ushidarena / the mountain of the good understanding
Yasna 44, 'the Questions to the Lord'

segments.name: The Revelation at the Waters, the vision of the Good Mind and the seven conferences

stops.name: The Daiti river at dawn, the vision of Vohu Manah at the spring festival, age thirty
stops.campa: At thirty, at the spring feast, he wades at daybreak into the mid-current of the Daiti to fetch the purest water for the haoma pressing. Coming up from the river he lifts his eyes and sees, on the bank, a shining being nine times the height of a man, radiant, clothed in light like silk: Vohu Manah, the Good Mind, the archangel of the Wise Lord. The angel bids him lay down his body and asks who he is and what he most desires. Righteousness, answers Zarathustra, and knowledge. Then Vohu Manah leads his soul away from the world of matter into the presence of the assembly of light.
stops.quote: With hands outstretched in reverence of him, our support, the spirit virtuous through truth, I first entreat all of you, Wise One, through this act.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.3 (the first revelation on the Daiti)
Nowruz, the vernal-equinox festival of the vision
Yasna 43, the Ushtavaiti Gatha of the calling

stops.name: Before the throne of Ahura Mazda, the Wise Lord and the declaration of the two Spirits
stops.campa: Vohu Manah brings him before Ahura Mazda and the radiant assembly. There Zarathustra casts no shadow, so great is the light. The Wise Lord reveals himself as the one uncreated Creator of all that is good, and unfolds to the prophet the secret of the cosmos: two primal Spirits, twins, who chose at the beginning, the one Life and the other Not-Life; the whole world a battlefield of Asha, the Truth, against Druj, the Lie. Every man and every angel must choose. The Wise Lord gives him the fire-faith to carry back to the creatures and the charge to summon them to the good side of the war.
stops.quote: Now the two primal Spirits, who reveal themselves in vision as Twins, are the Better and the Bad, in thought and word and action.
suggested_refs: The Ahunavaiti Gatha (Yasna 28-34)
Yasna 30, the choice of the two Spirits
Denkard VII (the conference with Ohrmazd)

stops.name: The seven conferences, the meetings with the Amesha Spentas over ten years
stops.campa: Over the following years the prophet is granted seven conferences with the divine beings, once for each of the Bounteous Immortals, the Amesha Spentas who are the very faces of the Wise Lord: Vohu Manah the Good Mind, Asha Vahishta the Best Truth, Khshathra the Kingdom, Spenta Armaiti holy Devotion, Haurvatat Wholeness and Ameretat Immortality. From each he receives a portion of the wisdom and a commandment for the good creation: the tending of cattle, the keeping of fire, the care of earth, water, plant and man. In these audiences the whole religion is given him, question by question, until the doctrine of the Good Religion stands complete.
stops.quote: As the holy one I conceived thee, Mazda Ahura, when I saw thee in the beginning at the birth of Life, when thou madest actions and words to have their meed — evil for the evil, a good destiny for the good.
suggested_refs: The Amesha Spentas, the seven Bounteous Immortals
Denkard VII.4 (the seven conferences)
The Yasna liturgy, the sevenfold structure of the divine world

stops.name: Mount Sabalan by Lake Urmia, the western tradition of the communing
stops.campa: Another line of the tradition sets the prophet's speaking with God not in the far northeast but in the northwest, in Media, in the land of Atropatene about Lake Urmia. There, on the high snows of Mount Sabalan above the lake, the seekers say Zarathustra withdrew to commune with Ahura Mazda and to receive the law, and there some hold him born, at Ragha the plain. The two homelands, east and west, are held together in the one faith: wherever the mountain, the vision is the same, the Good Mind meeting the prophet and leading him to the throne of light. The Iranian world keeps both cradles of its teacher.
suggested_refs: Mount Sabalan / Savalan, Azerbaijan, the western site of the communing
Lake Urmia and Atropatene, the northwestern birthplace tradition
Ragha (Rey) in Media, the alternate homeland

stops.name: The temptation of the demon, Angra Mainyu, on the mountain
stops.campa: The Evil Spirit, Angra Mainyu, learning that the doom of the demons is now spoken, sends his fiend to break the prophet. The demon offers him the lordship of the whole world if he will renounce the Good Religion. Zarathustra refuses, and answers the tempter with the great words of the faith, hurling the sacred formulas like stones the size of houses, and drives the demon back into the darkness. Even at the price of every bone in his body broken, he will not forsake the religion of the Wise Lord. The Lie recoils; the prophet holds the field.
stops.quote: Never shall I forsake the good Mazdayasnian Religion — not even if my life, my breath, and the very bones of my body should be broken.
suggested_refs: Vendidad 19 (the temptation of Zarathustra by Ahriman)
Denkard VII.4
The Fravarane, the profession of faith

segments.name: The Years of Preaching, the mockery, the one convert, and the road east

stops.name: Airyanem Vaejah, ten years preaching to the deaf, the one true word
stops.campa: He comes down from the mountain and preaches the Good Religion to his own people, and they will not hear. For ten years the priests and the princes mock him, drive him from their doors, set the mob against him. He wins not one soul. Alone with the Wise Lord he cries out his grief in the hymns, asking to what land he may flee, why he is thrust out, powerless, with few cattle and few men. Yet he does not turn back. The Truth is worth more than the whole world's scorn, and he keeps preaching to the deaf against the whole weight of the Lie.
stops.quote: To what land to flee? Whither shall I go to flee? They exclude me from my family and from my clan. Neither the community nor the wicked rulers of the land satisfy me.
suggested_refs: Yasna 46, the Gatha of exile and complaint
Denkard VII.4 (the ten fruitless years)

stops.name: The conversion of Maidhyoimanha, the cousin, the first believer, in the tenth year
stops.campa: In the tenth year of preaching the first man believes: his own cousin Maidhyoimanha, son of Arasti, who takes up the sacred girdle and professes the religion of the Wise Lord. One convert after ten years of scorn, and the prophet counts it a victory, for now the good side of the war has a second soldier in the world of men. To Maidhyoimanha he entrusts the faith, and the two go on together. From this single grain the whole harvest of the Good Religion will one day grow across the Iranian lands.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.4 (Maidhyoimanha the first convert)
Yasna 51.19, the naming of Maidhyoimanha in the Gathas

stops.name: The road to Bactra, the journey to the court of King Vishtaspa
stops.campa: Rejected by his own district, the prophet sets out for the great court of King Vishtaspa at Balkh, where the fate of the religion will be decided. He travels the roads of eastern Iran with Maidhyoimanha, carrying the fire and the word. If the king can be won, the whole realm will follow; the Good Religion needs a throne to stand on. He comes at last to the city of Bactra, mother of cities, where Vishtaspa reigns, and asks to be heard in the hall of the wise men, that he may set the doctrine of Ahura Mazda before the assembled learning of the kingdom.
suggested_refs: Balkh (Bactra), the capital of King Vishtaspa
Zardusht-nama (the journey to the court)
Shahnameh, the coming of Zardusht to Gushtasp

segments.name: The Court of Vishtaspa, the debates, the prison, and the miracle of the black horse

stops.name: The hall of the wise men, the great debate, thirty days and thirty nights
stops.campa: Before King Vishtaspa the prophet disputes with the assembled sages of the realm, the learned and the priests of the old worship, for many days. Question by question he overthrows them, until none can answer him and the whole learning of the court is silenced. The king is moved and inclines toward the new faith. But the jealous magi and karapans, seeing their power slipping, resolve to destroy the stranger by treachery, for they cannot beat him by argument. The truth has won the debate; now the Lie prepares its ambush in the dark.
stops.quote: Hear with your ears the best things; look upon them with clear-seeing thought, for decision between the two beliefs, each man for himself before the great consummation.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.4 (the disputation before Vishtaspa)
Shahnameh, Zardusht disputes at Gushtasp's court
Yasna 30, the Gatha of the two choices

stops.name: The dungeon of Vishtaspa, the false witchcraft and the imprisonment
stops.campa: The envious priests bribe the prophet's servant and plant in his chamber foul things: bones of dogs and cats, hair and clawings, the trappings of black witchcraft. Then they denounce him to the king as a sorcerer, and Vishtaspa, deceived, casts Zarathustra into a dark cell and cuts off his food. For days he lies chained in the dungeon, betrayed by the very lie he came to break. Yet he is not shaken; he waits on the Wise Lord, knowing that the Truth cannot be held long in the dark, and that the sign of his vindication is already being prepared in the king's own stables.
suggested_refs: Zardusht-nama (the imprisonment of Zardusht)
Denkard VII (the plot of the karapans)

stops.name: The black horse of the king, the four legs and the four requests
stops.campa: That morning the king's beloved black stallion is stricken: its four legs draw up and vanish into its belly, and no healer can help. From his cell Zarathustra sends word that he can cure it on four conditions, and as each is granted one leg is restored. First, that Vishtaspa accept the Good Religion; one leg shoots out. Second, that Prince Isfandiyar swear to defend the faith. Third, that Queen Hutaosa embrace it. Fourth, that the priests who framed him confess their lie, and the fourth leg is whole, the horse sound, the plot laid bare. The court kneels; the fire-religion is enthroned.
suggested_refs: Zardusht-nama, the miracle of the black horse Aspe-siha
Denkard VII.4 (the conversion of Vishtaspa)
Shahnameh, the conversion of Gushtasp

stops.name: The conversion of the house of Vishtaspa, the king, the queen, the prince and the sage
stops.campa: The whole royal house comes over to the Good Religion. To seal it, heaven sends four gifts and four wonders. Vishtaspa is given a cup and sees the glory of the world beyond and returns unafraid of death. The wise vizier Jamasp drinks and receives foresight and reads all that is to come. Prince Isfandiyar is made body-brazen, invulnerable in war. Prince Peshotan is granted deathlessness in the flesh. King and queen, prince and sage, all now stand within the war of the Truth, and the throne of Bactria becomes the seat of the fire-faith.
suggested_refs: Denkard VII.4-5 (the four wonders granted to the court)
Isfandiyar the brazen-bodied, Shahnameh
Jamasp the seer, the Jamasp Namag

segments.name: The Enthroned Faith, the fires, the scripture, and the household of the prophet

stops.name: The kindling of Adur Burzen-Mihr, the great fire on Mount Revand
stops.campa: With the king converted, Zarathustra and Vishtaspa kindle the sacred fires that will guard the realm. On Mount Revand in Khorasan the prophet establishes Adur Burzen-Mihr, the fire that needs no fuel and gives no smoke, the fire of the farmers and the herdsmen, one of the three great fires of the earth. Fire-altars rise across Iran, and the tending of the pure flame becomes the very center of the worship, the visible sign of Asha on earth. Where the flame burns, the Truth is present; the Wise Lord is served in light.
stops.quote: Truth is best of all that is good. As we desire, as we desire, may truth be ours.
suggested_refs: Adur Burzen-Mihr, one of the three Great Fires
Mount Revand, Khorasan (near Sabzevar)
The Ashem Vohu, the core Zoroastrian prayer of Truth

stops.name: The giving of the Avesta, the twenty-one Nasks and the tree of Kishmar
stops.campa: To the king the prophet gives the Avesta, the twenty-one Nasks written in letters of gold on ox-hides, the whole word of Ahura Mazda, among them the five Gathas: Ahunavaiti, Ushtavaiti, Spentomad, Vohukhshathra and Vahishtoisht. In sign of the covenant a cypress from paradise is planted at Kishmar, growing marvelously tall, with the words of the Good Religion inscribed upon its trunk. The scripture is laid up in the royal treasury, and the fire-faith now has its book, its liturgy and its law, established from the throne to the least village of the realm.
stops.quote: This I ask thee, tell me truly, Ahura. Who upholds the earth beneath and the firmament from falling? Who the waters and the plants? Who yoked swiftness to winds and clouds?
suggested_refs: The twenty-one Nasks of the Avesta
The Cypress of Kishmar (Kashmar), the paradise-tree of Zoroaster
The five Gathas, the prophet's own hymns

stops.name: The brothers of the court, the conversion of Frashaoshtra and Jamasp
stops.campa: Two noble brothers of the Hvogva house come to the faith and become the prophet's own pillars. Frashaoshtra gives his daughter Hvovi to Zarathustra to wife and stands as father-in-law of the religion; Jamasp the sage takes the daughter Pouruchista and becomes the prophet's foremost disciple, so gifted with foresight that the last things are unfolded to him and he foretells the whole course of the world down to the resurrection. The prophet names them in his own hymns as the men who choose the Good Mind. Around Vishtaspa's throne now stands a brotherhood of the faith, kinsmen bound by the Truth.
stops.quote: That man attains the best, who, being wise, tells me the true words concerning the Bridge of the Separator — even Zarathustra; kinsmen and followers, Frashaoshtra, will I lead across.
stops.quote_source: Gathas, Yasna 46.14-17 (theme of the named followers)
suggested_refs: Frashaoshtra and Jamasp of the Hvogva clan
The Jamasp Namag (the prophecies of Jamasp)
Yasna 46 and 51, the named disciples in the Gathas

stops.name: The threefold healing: the prophet teaches medicine by knife, herb and word
stops.campa: The prophet gives the world the arts of healing, for to keep the good creation whole is itself a war against the Lie that brings sickness and death. He teaches three medicines: healing by the knife, the surgeon's craft; healing by the herb, the virtue of the good plants the Wise Lord made; and healing by the holy word, the recited spell of the Manthra, which of the three is the most powerful, for it reaches the soul. The physician who heals with the sacred word heals best of all. So the faith takes the body as well as the soul into its care, against the demon of disease.
suggested_refs: Vendidad 7, the three healers (knife, herb, holy word)
Ancient Iranian medicine, the Manthra healing
The Ardibehesht Yasht (healing by the holy word)

stops.name: The marriage to Hvovi, the household and the children of the prophet
stops.campa: At the court the prophet takes to wife Hvovi, daughter of the noble Frashaoshtra, of the counselor-house of the kingdom. From his marriages come six children who will carry the seed of the religion: the sons Isadvastar, Urvatatnar and Khvarshedcheher, and the daughters Freni, Thriti and Pouruchista, the youngest, to whom he gives counsel in his own hymns when he weds her to the sage Jamasp. Around him now stands a household of the faith, a family of the Good Religion, and the prophet's line is set to run down the ages toward the Saviors who are to come.
stops.quote: This is well known to the wooers and to thee, O Pouruchista, youngest of the daughters of Zarathustra: he gives thee as a helpmate one who is strong in the Good Mind and in Truth.
stops.quote_source: Gathas, Yasna 53.3 (paraphrase of the Vahishtoisht Gatha)
suggested_refs: Yasna 53, the wedding hymn for Pouruchista
Frashaoshtra and Jamasp, the brothers of the court
Denkard VII (the family of Zarathustra)

segments.name: The Holy Wars and the Last Things, Turan, the Bridge, the Saviour, and the fire-altar

stops.name: The seven regions, the sending-out of the faith and the feast of the new day
stops.campa: From the throne of Bactria the Good Religion goes out to the seven climes of the earth. The prophet sends teachers and priests across the Iranian lands, and the fire-altars multiply from Chorasmia to Sistan. He hallows the turning of the year: at the vernal equinox, when day conquers night, the feast of Nowruz is kept, the new day, sign and rehearsal of the last renewal of the world, when the Wise Lord will make all things wonderful. The whole ordered year becomes a liturgy of the war of light, each festival a station on the road from the first creation to the Making-Wonderful at the end.
stops.quote: May we be those who shall make this world wonderful, when it shall be renewed — we, the saviours of the world, through the will of the Wise Lord.
suggested_refs: Nowruz, the Zoroastrian new-year of the renewal
Frashokereti, the Making-Wonderful at the end of time
The seven karshvars (climes) of the Avestan earth

stops.name: The first war against Arjasp of Turan, the demand and the battle
stops.campa: Arjasp, king of Turan and champion of the demon-worship, sends to Vishtaspa demanding that he abandon the Good Religion and return to the old idols, or face war. On the prophet's counsel the king refuses. The Turanian hosts pour into Iran, and a terrible battle is joined. Vishtaspa's brother Zarir falls in the field, and the aged Lohrasp with him; but Prince Isfandiyar, brazen-bodied and unconquerable, breaks the enemy and drives Arjasp back beyond the river. The first holy war is won, and the fire-faith stands defended by the sword as well as the word.
suggested_refs: The Ayadgar i Zareran (the Memorial of Zarir), the epic of the holy war
Shahnameh, the wars of Gushtasp and Arjasp
Isfandiyar's campaigns

stops.name: The Bridge of the Separator, the Chinvat and the judgment of souls
stops.campa: The prophet teaches the last things. At death every soul waits three days by the body, and on the fourth dawn comes to the Chinvat Bridge, the Bridge of the Separator, where its deeds are weighed. To the just the bridge grows broad, and a fair maiden, the soul's own good conscience, leads it to the House of Song, the paradise of light. To the wicked the bridge narrows to a razor's edge, a foul hag meets it, and it falls into the House of the Lie. Those whose good and ill are equal wait in Hamistagan between. Every choice in life is met again at the Bridge.
stops.quote: When shall I know, O Wise One, that ye have power over any whom my tongue threatens? Let the reward of the followers of Truth be told me.
suggested_refs: The Chinvat Bridge, the Bridge of the Separator
The maiden of good conscience (the Daena)
Videvdad 19 and the Hadokht Nask (the fate of the soul)

stops.name: Lake Kansaoya, the seed of the prophet and the Saviour to come
stops.campa: The prophet reveals the end of the world. His own seed is kept, guarded by thousands of holy spirits, in the waters of Lake Kansaoya in the land of the lake-basin. At the last times, in three appointed ages, three Saviours will be born of it: a virgin will bathe in the miraculous water, conceive by the seed of Zarathustra, and bear the Saoshyant, the last Saviour, who will raise the dead, make the molten metal flow like warm milk over the good, put down the demon and the Lie forever, and renew the whole world in the Making-Wonderful. The prophet's line reaches to the resurrection itself.
suggested_refs: Lake Kansaoya / Hamun-e Helmand (Sistan), the lake of the seed
The three Saoshyants, the Saviours to come
The Frashokereti, the final renovation of the world

stops.name: The second war and the sack of Balkh: Arjasp returns
stops.campa: After long peace Arjasp of Turan gathers his hosts again and, while Isfandiyar is away or in chains, falls upon Bactra by surprise. The Turanians storm the city, mother of cities, and put it to fire and sword. They break into the great temple where the sacred fire burns and slaughter the priests of the Good Religion at their altars. The aged prophet, now seventy-seven years old, is within, keeping the fire of Nush-Adar. The Lie has come at last with an army to the very sanctuary of the Truth.
suggested_refs: Shahnameh, the second war of Arjasp and the sack of Balkh
Ayadgar i Zareran
Balkh, the fire-temple of Nush-Adar

stops.name: The fire-altar of Nush-Adar, the death of the prophet at seventy-seven
stops.campa: At the fire-altar in Balkh, praying before the flame, the prophet is struck down. A Turanian of the old enemy, the karapan Bradres, the very kind of sorcerer who tried to kill him at his birth, comes on him from behind and slays him at the fire he has tended all his life, in the seventy-seventh year of his age. As he falls he hurls his rosary at the murderer, who dies of it; the Truth is not defenceless even in death. So the one who laughed at his birth dies at his altar and passes over his own Bridge into the House of Song.
